observation.description: In a sessions-mode app, a plain declarative live query over a public table (no auth gate, no membership, no authScopeField) is still treated as authority-scoped: the handle reports retention {retainable:false, code:SNAPBACK_RETENTION_NOT_RETAINABLE} and nothing ever persists — the shipped sync.offline-js-arm cold-boot claim silently never engages for the whole app. The opt-in that makes a query rqsEligible is declaring auth:'public' + authorityIndependent:true (+ retainable:true) on the query, learned from packaged define.mjs bytes. The offline guide page (sync/offline-and-retention.md) says 'authority-independent live queries' retain but never shows how a query becomes authority-independent; 'retainable' appears nowhere in the guide as an author-facing flag; the only authorityIndependent example lives in the unrelated snapshot-bundles page. A consumer building the guide's own offline story cannot find the declaration that turns it on.
evidence: demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a1-snapback-web/evidence/phase-warm.json (pre-fix run retained in git history; final run shows sites retainable:true after the flags)

competitorOutcome.description: Firebase's offline persistence is one client-construction decision (persistentLocalCache) covering every query including protected ones; the frozen Diary 0027 Firebase arm passed durable cold offline boot with no per-query declarations.

mustNotRegress: The refuse-with-clarity handle facts (retention.code/reason naming the boundary) — the docs fix must not paper over the honest refusal.
smallestCoherentFix: Teach the retainability opt-in on the offline page (and the queries page's declarative spec table): which flags make a query rqsEligible, what each implies, and a CI-verified snippet whose handle reports retainable:true.
acceptanceWitness: A cold agent reading only guide/sync/offline-and-retention.md authors a sessions-mode app whose public reference query cold-retains on the first try.
